summary: Hypothesis-only demo: validate whether solo SaaS founders want a lightweight in-app feedback widget before spending anything on distribution. Start with participation-first founder communities, because they are free and give feedback within days.
biggest_uncertainty: Founders may already be 'good enough' with a free form or a shared inbox, which would make the pain real but unpaid.

snapshot.problem: Small SaaS teams hear about problems late, because feedback tools are heavy to set up.
snapshot.promise: Collect meaningful in-app feedback in minutes, without a heavyweight tool.
snapshot.differentiation: Setup time measured in minutes, not days.

icps.name: Solo SaaS founder with 50-500 users
icps.job_to_be_done: Learn why users churn or get stuck without running surveys by hand
icps.trigger: A churn spike or a support thread that reveals a missing feature
icps.alternatives: Email, Typeform, a shared inbox, a free feedback board
icps.objections: One more script on my site; I can ask users by email

icps.name: Product-minded developer at a 3-10 person startup
icps.job_to_be_done: Give the team a lightweight channel for user voice
icps.trigger: First hire in support or product
icps.objections: We already pay for a support tool

disconfirming: Free alternatives (a form plus a spreadsheet) may be good enough for most solo founders.
Open question: do founders at this size act on in-app feedback, or does their volume stay too low for a tool to matter?

channels.name: Founder communities (participation-first)
channels.rationale: Fast qualitative feedback from the exact ICP, if the founder has standing.
channels.effort: Medium: daily presence for two weeks
channels.rule: Check each community's current promotion rules

channels.name: Content on collecting feedback
channels.rationale: Compounding search reach, but slow validation.
channels.effort: High: one useful post per week

channels.name: Launch directories
channels.rationale: A spike of visits, mostly other makers, not buyers.

channels.name: Subreddit that bans tool promotion
channels.rationale: Great place to learn what people complain about.
channels.rule: Hypothetical: rules prohibit self-promotion, so listen and help only

weeks.objective: Confirm the pain and the promise
actions: Hold five short conversations with target founders
weeks.signal: At least 3 of 5 describe the pain without being prompted
weeks.gate: Fewer than 2 confirm: change the ICP before building more

actions: Share one useful post where allowed
weeks.gate: No qualified replies after a fair attempt: change the message, not the volume

actions: Simplify installation based on demo friction
weeks.gate: Add channel #3 only if one channel produced signal
No channel has signal: pause and revisit the ICP

copy.positioning: For solo SaaS founders who learn about problems too late, FormNest is a lightweight feedback widget that installs in minutes, unlike heavy tools that need a sprint to set up.
hooks: You find out why users left three weeks after they left.
Hear from users inside your app, with five minutes of setup.
Not another feedback suite: one widget, one inbox.
copy.launch_post:
I built FormNest, a small feedback widget for solo SaaS apps.
It's in private beta and still rough around onboarding.
I'm looking for 5 founders who'd try it and tell me what's missing.
copy.reply_draft: The trade-off with feedback tools is usually setup time versus workflow depth. What matters most for your app right now? (Disclosure: I'm building a small tool in this space.)

experiments.hypothesis: Target founders describe late feedback as a real pain without prompting
experiments.test: Five 15-minute calls with founders found in communities where they already talk about the topic
experiments.kpi: Calls where the pain is raised unprompted
experiments.decision_gate: Proposed: 3 of 5 continue, fewer than 2 means change the ICP

experiments.hypothesis: Promise A ('know why users leave') beats promise B ('five-minute setup')
experiments.test: Two headlines shown to opt-in beta visitors
experiments.decision_gate: Proposed: review after 100 visitors per variant; a clear gap decides

experiments.hypothesis: A useful founder-community post produces qualified conversations
experiments.test: One educational post where allowed, then reply to every comment
experiments.decision_gate: Proposed: 3 qualified conversations continues the channel

experiments.test: Compare the current onboarding with a concierge setup for opt-in testers

experiments.hypothesis: Founders will commit to pay before the product is finished
experiments.test: Offer a discounted founding-member price to active testers

risks: The problem may be too low priority for solo founders.
Free alternatives may be good enough.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 3 of 10 target conversations confirm the pain unprompted.
Zero qualified replies from the top two channels after a fair attempt.
next_action: Within 48 hours, message five founders you already know and ask for a 15-minute call about how they collect feedback today.
